claims.statement: pnpm-workspace.yaml declares the glob roots apps/* and packages/*, yielding exactly four workspaces: apps/web (@mota/web, React 19 + Vite PWA), apps/api (@mota/api, NestJS 11 on Fastify), packages/contracts (@mota/contracts, shared Zod schemas), and packages/db (@mota/db, Drizzle ORM for PostgreSQL).

Only apps/api is started in production; the container command is `node apps/api/dist/main.js`, and apps/web is built by Vite to static assets served by the Nest app from the same container. In development the two apps meet only at the HTTP boundary, with the Vite dev server proxying /api to http://127.0.0.1:3000.

packages/contracts imports only Zod and its own modules: its sole runtime dependency is zod, and every source file imports either `zod` or a sibling module such as ./bus and ./subway, which keeps the package usable from both the browser bundle and Node.

packages/db imports only @mota/contracts and Drizzle (drizzle-orm, postgres) and never imports Nest or React; the API consumes the database exclusively through the UserSettingsRepository interface that @mota/db exports, so Drizzle never leaks past the db boundary.
The two apps never import each other: @mota/web depends on @mota/contracts but not on @mota/db, so the browser bundle cannot transitively reach Drizzle, Postgres code, or any server-side module.

Inside apps/web the contracts package is re-exported once through apps/web/src/domain/bus.ts and apps/web/src/domain/subway.ts (`export * from "@mota/contracts/bus"` and the subway equivalent), so component code never names the package directly.

pnpm-workspace.yaml sets injectWorkspacePackages: true and nodeLinker: hoisted; combined with workspace:* specifiers this links the shared packages into each dependent's node_modules (the lockfile records link:../../packages/contracts and link:../contracts) and produces a flat root node_modules that lets the Docker runtime image copy one tree plus two manual symlinks instead of reinstalling.

pnpm-workspace.yaml gates native postinstall scripts to exactly four packages via allowBuilds/onlyBuiltDependencies — @nestjs/core, @scarf/scarf, @swc/core, and esbuild — so no other package runs install-time code.

apps/web/vite.config.ts installs two resolve aliases — the more specific @mota/contracts/transit-settings to ../../packages/contracts/src/transitSettings.ts first, then @mota/contracts to ../../packages/contracts/src — so the Vite dev server and production bundle consume the contracts TypeScript source compiled inline rather than the package's compiled dist, and a schema change is visible to the web app without building packages/contracts.

apps/web/tsconfig.json mirrors the Vite aliases as compilerOptions.paths (@mota/contracts, @mota/contracts/transit-settings, and @mota/contracts/* all pointing into ../../packages/contracts/src), so tsc --noEmit typechecks web code against the same source files the bundler resolves; the alias pair and the paths pair must stay in sync.

apps/api and packages/db have no path mappings and resolve @mota/contracts through the node_modules symlink and the package's exports map, which points at ./dist — which is why the package build must run before the API can typecheck or test, and turbo's ^build dependency guarantees packages/contracts/dist exists first.

The Docker build compiles both packages with tsc explicitly (tsc -p packages/contracts/tsconfig.build.json and tsc -p packages/db/tsconfig.build.json, which turn noEmit off, emit declarations and source maps, and exclude tests), then builds apps/web with vite and apps/api with nest; the runtime stage copies node_modules, each package's package.json + dist, the web bundle to /app/web, and the Drizzle SQL to /app/drizzle, and finally recreates the pnpm links by hand with `ln -s ../../packages/contracts node_modules/@mota/contracts` and `ln -s ../../packages/db node_modules/@mota/db`.

In turbo.json the build, typecheck, test, test:integration, and dev tasks all declare dependsOn ["^build"], so the package builds always run before any app task and @mota/contracts and @mota/db have fresh dist output when app tasks start; build is cached on outputs dist/** and test on coverage/**.

test:integration sets cache: false and env: ["DATABASE_URL"] because it exercises a real Postgres database and is never replayed from cache; its two entry points (apps/api test/settings.postgres.integration.test.ts and packages/db src/repository.integration.test.ts) wrap their suites in describe.runIf(Boolean(process.env.DATABASE_URL)), so the task is a silent no-op when no database URL is exported rather than failing.

The dev task sets cache: false and persistent: true, so `turbo run dev` fans out to the Vite dev server and `nest start --watch` and stays attached without turbo terminating the watchers; the root scripts scope it with `turbo run dev --filter=@mota/web` (pnpm dev:web) and `--filter=@mota/api` (pnpm dev:api), and ^build still applies so the packages are compiled before either watcher starts.

Root package.json scripts split into turbo-delegated tasks (dev, build, typecheck, check, test, test:integration as `turbo run ...`) and single-workspace commands that bypass turbo using `pnpm --filter` (db:generate, db:migrate, db:studio against @mota/db; test:watch and test:e2e against @mota/web).

tsconfig.base.json pins the shared language level and strictness for all four workspaces: target ES2022, strict, skipLibCheck, forceConsistentCasingInFileNames, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and useUnknownInCatchVariables; each workspace extends it and adds only its module world (apps/web uses ESNext/Bundler with DOM libs and JSX, apps/api uses Node16 with decorators and outDir dist, packages/contracts uses CommonJS/Node, packages/db uses Node16 with node types).

A single root biome.json carries the formatting contract (2-space indent, 100-column width, double quotes, semicolons) and the recommended lint preset, scanning everything except node_modules, dist, coverage, and .omo; each workspace's check script invokes `biome lint` with an explicit path list, and there is no ESLint, Prettier, or Jest anywhere in the repository.

apps/api/biome.json is the only Biome override in the repo: it declares "root": false, extends ../../biome.json, enables unsafeParameterDecoratorsEnabled for Nest's constructor-parameter decorators, and turns off the correctness/noUnusedFunctionParameters rule.

All three test-bearing workspaces use Vitest with plain per-file configuration: apps/api and packages/db run in the default node environment (apps/api/vitest.config.mts includes src/** and test/**), while every web test file opts into jsdom individually via a `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma and apps/web/vitest.setup.ts wires Testing Library cleanup plus jest-dom matchers.

@mota/contracts is the only code shared between the two apps and the single choke point for cross-system types: both apps and packages/db declare it as a workspace:* dependency, and every cross-boundary type (transit selections, bus/subway schemas, auth user) is defined there.
